title: edge-rollout-tactical-notes-ak
content:
Quick personal scratchpad for an edge-region canary rollout (notes, commands, TODOs). Rough and messy — meant for my own brain dump before I formalize a runbook.

Context:
- Goal: roll out v2.1.0-quant to europe-west-edge cluster (reduced batch size profile) and gradually shift 5% -> 20% -> 50% if latency/cost/QA stable.
- Motivation: 2.1.0 reduces token cost ~12% with 8-bit kernels but regresses avg 99th pct latency if sequence length > 512. Need cautious canary.

Preflight checklist (quick):
- [ ] Build image tag: redwood/serve:v2.1.0-quant-20251102 (verify digest)
- [ ] Confirm model artifact checksum in S3 (s3://redwood-models/ops/2.1.0/sha256:abcd1234)
- [ ] Canary config stored in k8s preview namespace: rollout/edge-eu-canary (do NOT apply to prod yet)
- [ ] Monitoring dashboards: open "eu-edge/canary-latency" and "token-cost-by-route" in Console
- [ ] Slack channel #prod-rollouts notified with plan + timestamp

Tactical steps (order-of-ops):
1) Create a small canary service in eu-edge with 3 pods (minReplicas=3) and resource limit tuned to current steady-state. Use dedicated node pool (np-edge-small).
   - kubectl apply -f manifests/canary-v2.1.0-eu.yaml --context=gke-eu-edge
2) Pin route /v1/generate to canary via traffic-split: 95% -> stable (v2.0.x), 5% -> canary (v2.1.0-quant)
   - curl -X POST $ADMIN_URL/traffic-split -d '{"route":"/v1/generate","splits":[{"version":"v2.0.x","pct":95},{"version":"v2.1.0-quant","pct":5}]}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN"
3) Smoke tests (automated): run local harness against canary pods with seq len distribution: [32,128,256,600]
   - ./tools/harness --target eu-edge-canary --concurrency 4 --payloads tests/prompt-mix-small.json
   - Fail criteria: error-rate > 0.5% OR p99 latency increase > 15% vs baseline OR perplexity/quality sentinel drop > threshold
4) Observe 30–60m: watch for OOMs, retry spikes, L7 5xx, increased disk IO. If anything looks bad -> rollback to v2.0.x immediately (see rollback steps).
5) If stable -> increase to 20% for next 2 hours, repeat checks. Then 50% for 4 hours before full cutover.

Rollbacks & kill-switches (emergency):
- Quick route revert: POST to admin traffic-split with 100% to stable. This is fastest and safest. Keep command in pinned Slack message.
- Node-pool drain: kubectl scale --replicas=0 deployment/eu-edge-canary -n canary-preview (works if want to stop traffic quickly but leaves routing config confused).
- If bad memory/regression: SSH to pod to capture core dump + top, then kubectl logs --since=10m to capture tail errors.

Metrics to monitor (primary):
- p95, p99 latency by route (gen/chat), by seq_len bucket
- error rate (5xx and 429)
- queue time / batching size distribution (shouldn't spike)
- GPU utilization and per-token cost estimate (Console: token-cost-by-route)
- Quality signals: BLEU-like heuristics for eval prompts, plus manual sampling of 50 responses per interval

Notes to self / heuristics:
- If p99 up but p95 stable and no errors: maybe cold-starts or one-off long contexts. Watch sequence length distribution.
- If cost drops but quality regressions appear in certain prompts (long completion truncation) -> consider pinned model for routes that need long contexts (e.g., /summarize).
- Prefer traffic-split route changes over deployment-scale toggles — fewer moving parts for rollback.

Local troubleshooting commands (cheat):
- List canary pods: kubectl get pods -n canary-preview -l app=serve-canary -o wide
- Exec into pod: kubectl exec -it pod/serve-canary-0 -n canary-preview -- /bin/bash
- Fetch recent logs: kubectl logs pod/serve-canary-0 -n canary-preview --tail=500
- Run harness against single pod: ./tools/harness --pod serve-canary-0 --requests 200 --payload tests/prompt-mix-small.json

Open questions / TODOs (write down for follow-up):
- Q: Is there a per-route pin API in the console yet? If not, file a small feature request: CONSOLE-REQ-78.
- Q: Does Dedicated capacity respect 8-bit kernels the same way? Confirm with infra (Rahul) before mass rollouts.
- TODO: Add a lightweight canary-liveness probe that samples a few long-seq prompts at pod startup (so we catch p99 regressions earlier).
- TODO: Draft a short one-pager for CS about differences when we pin quantized models (explain perf/quality trade-offs).

Quick timeline suggestion (today):
- 09:00 — Preflight + notify
- 09:30 — Deploy canary pods (3)
- 09:45 — Apply 5% traffic split
- 10:15 — First smoke test batch + check dashboards
- 12:00 — If stable, move to 20% and loop until 50% by EOD (only if metrics stay green)

Random notes / partial thoughts (brain dump):
- Might be worth a small script that diffs kernel lists between versions to show which optimized paths changed. Saves time when answering why p99 regressed.
- Keep a pinned sample set of "long context" prompts for each app team we support. When doing a canary, run those first.

Slack snippets to copy/paste (for notify):
- "Planning canary rollout of v2.1.0-quant to eu-edge today. Starting 09:30 with 5% traffic. Watch eu-edge/canary-latency and token-cost-by-route. Ping @rahul if you see anything before 10:30."

End of scratchpad. Will clean into a formal runbook if this goes smoothly.

-- Alex K.
